LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 9.3.1 SENTENCES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How can we achieve sentence variety in communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explain the basic rules of subject- verb agreement in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. examine the agreement of subject-verb in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. distinguish between active and passive sentences in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. construct active and passive sentences for variety in communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. advocate for the use of a variety of sentences for effective communication. ● in pairs, learners are guided to brainstorm the rules governing subject- verb agreement, ● in groups, learners are guided to read a text and list sentences in which the subject and the verb are singular, ● in groups, learners are guided to work with others to change each of the sentences into its plural counterpart, ● in pairs, learners are guided to search online using digital devices with assistive technology and offline for the difference between active and passive sentences, How can we achieve sentence variety in communication? 112 ● in groups, learners are guided to generate sentences using singular and plural subjects and verbs, ● in groups, learners are guided to listen to an audio recording on the theme and pick out active and passive sentences, ● in groups, learners are guided to write a paragraph on the theme using active and passive sentences that observe subject-verb agreement.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. explain the basic rules of subject- verb agreement in sentences,

   Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. examine the agreement of subject-verb in sentences,

   Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. distinguish between active and passive sentences in a text,

   Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. construct active and passive sentences for variety in communication,

   Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. advocate for the use of a variety of sentences for effective communication. ● in pairs, learners are guided to brainstorm the rules governing subject- verb agreement, ● in groups, learners are guided to read a text and list sentences in which the subject and the verb are singular, ● in groups, learners are guided to work with others to change each of the sentences into its plural counterpart, ● in pairs, learners are guided to search online using digital devices with assistive technology and offline for the difference between active and passive sentences, How can we achieve sentence variety in communication? 112 ● in groups, learners are guided to generate sentences using singular and plural subjects and verbs, ● in groups, learners are guided to listen to an audio recording on the theme and pick out active and passive sentences, ● in groups, learners are guided to write a paragraph on the theme using active and passive sentences that observe subject-verb agreement.

   Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 9.3.1 Sentences together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem Solving: The learner exhibits open mindedness and creativity as they brainstorm the rules

governing subject-verb agreement.

Values:
Peace: The learner respects diversity as they work with others to change each of the sentences into its plural counterpart.

113

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education – Coping with emotion: The learner’s ability to deal with emotions is inculcated as they brainstorm the

rules governing subject-verb agreement.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print texts

● Braille texts

● Electronic reading materials

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Audio visual clips

Suggested Skills:

● Distinguish between active and passive sentences in a text

● Use a variety of sentences for effective communication.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. explain the basic rules of subject- verb agreement in sentences,
2. examine the agreement of subject-verb in sentences,
3. distinguish between active and passive sentences in a text,
4. construct active and passive sentences for variety in communication,
5. advocate for the use of a variety of sentences for effective communication. ● in pairs, learners are guided to brainstorm the rules governing subject- verb agreement, ● in groups, learners are guided to read a text and list sentences in which the subject and the verb are singular, ● in groups, learners are guided to work with others to change each of the sentences into its plural counterpart, ● in pairs, learners are guided to search online using digital devices with assistive technology and offline for the difference between active and passive sentences, How can we achieve sentence variety in communication? 112 ● in groups, learners are guided to generate sentences using singular and plural subjects and verbs, ● in groups, learners are guided to listen to an audio recording on the theme and pick out active and passive sentences, ● in groups, learners are guided to write a paragraph on the theme using active and passive sentences that observe subject-verb agreement.

Remember the key question: How can we achieve sentence variety in communication?
